subject: 93ADDD447B4E489DB8D200F294BCBEF8
introduction: “The Word of God may be likened unto a sapling, whose roots have been implanted in the hearts of men.” To “exalt the Word” is the writings’ usual phrase for teaching the Faith, and the guide follows it from that image of Bahá’u’lláh through ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s encouragements to Shoghi Effendi’s advice that the surest teaching is the text itself. The Bible’s confidence in the word is close at hand: it does “not return void”, it is “like as a fire”, it “shall stand for ever”; the Qur’an’s parable of the goodly word as a goodly tree is the very image of reading 1. Paul’s “not in word, but in power”, the Preacher’s “time to keep silence” and Emerson’s contempt for borrowed speech test the emphasis.
questions: What does it mean to “exalt” a word? How is that different from repeating it?
Reading 25 advises teaching by the actual words of the text. What are the strengths and the risks of that method?
Paul says the kingdom is “not in word, but in power”. Reading 4 says to live so as not to lower the Cause. How much of teaching is speech?
When is silence the wiser course?

outside.why: The Word is a sapling rooted in the heart. A goodly saying, as a goodly tree, its root set firm, its branches reaching into heaven.
And the parable in which the word is seed: other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit.
Ponder the methods of teaching, and learn the texts. Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
The Psalmist on learning the text by heart: thy word have I hid in mine heart.
“The hosts of wisdom and utterance.” Call unto the way of thy Lord with wisdom and fair exhortation.
Live so as not to lower the station of the Cause. That they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things.
Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father.
That the disturbed may find peace. That I should know how to speak a word in season to him that is weary.
The source of courage and power is promoting the Word. Is not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?
Strength that the world’s tribulations may not hinder us. Grant unto thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak thy word.
A world of striving is needed. How shall they hear without a preacher?
Strive that the Word be exalted. My word shall not return unto me void, but it shall accomplish that which I please.
Today is the day. Preach the word; be instant in season, out of season.
Every action that elevates the Word is good. The kingdom of God is not in word, but in power. How do the readings relate speaking the Word to living it?
Today is the time for teaching, and whoever arises will be assisted. Go ye therefore, and teach all nations: and, lo, I am with you alway.
“At all times hold fast unto wisdom.” A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in pictures of silver.
The Preacher allows what a zealous teacher does not: a time to keep silence, and a time to speak. Do readings 13 and 21 agree about when the Word should not be offered?
Give the people the joyful tidings. How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings.
Be not dismayed when the day-star of My beauty is set. The grass withereth, the flower fadeth: but the word of our God shall stand for ever.
To refute what is false and establish the truth. Be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you, with meekness.
Teach by the actual words of Bahá’u’lláh, which saves the Cause from misrepresentation. Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it.
Our own explanations are to be offered as such. In Paul’s epistles, Peter says, are some things hard to be understood, which the unlearned wrest.
Always the Word itself, not our version. Emerson would have a speaker say only what is his own: imitation is suicide. What place do the readings leave for the teacher’s own voice?
Imparting the holy words directly. Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

shortfall: Readings 6, 8, 10, 14, 15, 17, 18, 20 and 28 use the phrase “exalting the Word of God” without adding to it.

titus-adorn-the-doctrine.text: Not purloining, but shewing all good fidelity; that they may adorn the doctrine of God our Saviour in all things

acts-speak-thy-word-with-boldness.text: And now, Lord, behold their threatenings: and grant unto thy servants, that with all boldness they may speak thy word
